data.short_meaning: Goddess of wealth, abundance, and prosperity
data.long_meaning: Goddess of wealth, abundance, prosperity, and fertility. She is believed to bestow material and spiritual wealth upon her devotees. In Hindu mythology, Vasundhara is depicted as the queen of the earth, sitting on a lotus, surrounded by seven rivers and holding a golden lotus in her hand. The name Vasundhara carries the meaning “Goddess of wealth, abundance, and prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Vasundhara usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth, abundance, and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vasundhara total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Vasundhara" holds a significant cultural impact in Hinduism as it represents the goddess revered as the embodiment of wealth and prosperity. In various Hindu rituals and ceremonies, invocations to Goddess Vasundhara are made to seek her blessings for financial gains and material prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Vasundhara" symbolizes the abundant wealth and abundance that exists beyond physical wealth. It is believed that Goddess Vasundhara bestows her blessings to help her devotees achieve inner peace, contentment, and spiritual growth, ultimately leading to true wealth and prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vasundhara symbolizes abundance and prosperity, representing the Earth as a giver of all riches and blessings. Her name, derived from the Sanskrit words 'vasu' (abode) and 'dhara' (bearer), signifies the nurturing Earth that sustains and supports all life.

vedic_reference.note: Vasundhara is a prominent goddess in Hindu mythology, often invoked for wealth and prosperity. She is mentioned in various Vedic texts, including the Rigveda and the Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: Vasundhara was the name of the goddess of the Saraswati river, revered by the Vedic people around 1500 BCE. She was often depicted as a beautiful woman seated on a lotus, holding a water pot in her hand.

The name Vasundhara became popular in the 6th century CE during the Gupta Empire when it was used to refer to a specific form of the goddess Lakshmi. She was depicted as a lotus throne upon which the god Vishnu sat, symbolizing abundance and prosperity.
